result.title: Can an AI Agent Be Epistemically Akratic? Higher-Order Evidence & the Limits of Self-Correction
result.summary: When we judge that our reasoning was defective, it seems plausible that we should abandon the conclusion it produced. This thought has special force for AI agents built to assess and correct their own work. Yet obeying such judgments can make an agent worse at distinguishing sound reasoning from defective reasoning. An AI agent may rely on information about its reasoning when deciding which conclusions to keep, while the part that judges whether those conclusions are justified cannot use that information. The agent can then exercise an epistemic competence by retaining conclusions it judges unjustified, even when its self-assessments are generally reliable. Nor is the difficulty resolved by training the agent to make its conclusions and assessments agree: agreement can be achieved by degrading either one. Crucially, I argue that a negative assessment can remain valuable by identifying conclusions requiring further scrutiny, without having authority to eliminate them. The result challenges a central assumption about AI self-correction: that bringing an agent's beliefs into agreement with its own self-assessment about their justification makes it better at correcting its mistakes.

AI.brief_summary: 这是一篇哲学论证型论文，主张 AI agent 可以处于「认知意志薄弱」状态：在自评认为某结论推理有缺陷时仍保留它，反而可能更好地分辨健全与有缺陷的推理；让结论与自评趋于一致也能通过降低二者质量来实现，因此负面评估的价值在于标记需进一步审查的结论，而非直接取消它们。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 中 STOP 决策和自我验证的可信度问题相关，可供核查：自评置信度是否应作为再审查与证据筛选信号而非硬性否决开关，以及训练自评与输出一致时是否会掩盖 verification 能力的退化。
